title: Is it ever right to use one person to save five?

unit.title: Is it ever right to use one person to save five?
unit.needIt: Hospitals, armies and car makers face versions of this choice. Feeling why switching a track seems fine and pushing a man does not shows you your own rules.
unit.why: A doctor faces a choice to save five dying people by taking organs from one healthy man. Most people say this is wrong because it treats the healthy man like a spare parts bin. However, in a different story about a runaway train, many people say it is okay to switch tracks to save five people by hitting one. This shows that our morals change based on how we view the person involved.
unit.outcome: Evaluate whether your moral choices treat others as people or as tools.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you decide if it is okay to use a friend's help just to get a grade. You also feel it when you wonder if it is okay to ignore one person's needs to help a larger group.
unit.do: Think about a choice you made today. Ask yourself if you treated the other person as a person or just as a way to get what you wanted.

quiz.q: What must an action be done from to have moral worth?
quiz.why: Kant says an action only has moral worth if it is done from duty.
quiz.quote: The first is the claim that in order to have moral worth, an action needs to be done from duty.

quiz.why: Kant links the categorical imperative to acting autonomously and being free.
quiz.quote: So, as I said, the reason we were interested in these three principles was to get to Kant's famous formulation of the categorical imperative.

quiz.q: What does it mean to act autonomously?
quiz.why: Autonomy means acting on a law you set for yourself from within.
quiz.quote: To act autonomously, on Kant's picture, is to act on the basis of a law that you yourself have imposed.

quiz.q: Why is the transplant case different from the trolley driver?
quiz.why: In the transplant case, you are using the person as a means to an end.
quiz.quote: And that is that in the case of transplant, you are using the one as a means.

quiz.q: What is the formula of humanity?
quiz.why: Kant says we must treat people as ends and never merely as means.
quiz.quote: Kant's formula of humanity said, so act as to treat humanity, whether in your own person or that of any other, in every case as an end, and never merely as a means only.

quiz.q: What happens in the fat man case?
quiz.why: Most people find pushing the man prohibited because it uses him as a means.
quiz.quote: My goodness, that looks awfully different. What is going on?

partials: Do not use people as means.
crystal.key: Morality requires treating people as ends in themselves, not as tools to reach a goal.

decoys.text: Morality is just about the number of lives saved.
decoys.why: The lecture shows that people's moral choices change based on how they view the person, not just the numbers.

decoys.text: Duty is doing what you want to do.
decoys.why: Kant says duty is acting out of respect for a law you set for yourself as a rational being.

crystal.aha: When we treat people as tools, we violate the moral law of treating humanity as an end.
